details.note: Presence is checked; the values are not verified.

checks.name: Train accuracy minus eval accuracy (needs train metrics)
checks.message: Declared training accuracy 0.978 vs measured evaluation accuracy 0.978: gap +0.001. The training value is the producer's claim and was not verified.

checks.name: Eval rows that also appear in training data (needs row hashes)
checks.message: 12 of 9768 evaluation rows (0.12%) also appear in the training row hashes. Datasets can contain genuine duplicate records (0.03% of evaluation rows duplicate another evaluation row), so a small overlap is not by itself leakage. The hashes are producer-supplied.

checks.name: Highest ROC AUC reached by any single feature on eval data
checks.message: The strongest single feature, 'prior_high_income_flag', reaches a cross-validated ROC AUC of 0.968 on its own (13 features, 9768 rows). Values near 1.0 suggest the feature leaks the label.

details.caveat: A legitimately strong feature also scores high; leakage spread over several features is not detected.

checks.name: Evaluation rows whose features are identical to another row's but whose label differs
checks.message: 0 of 9768 evaluation rows (0.00%) share their feature values with a row that has a different label (0 conflicting groups among 2 groups of repeated feature values). Conflicting labels put a ceiling on the accuracy any model can reach and make the measured metrics unreliable.

details.caveat: Only exact repeats of the feature values are found, so data with continuous features has little power; the gate cannot check the training labels, which it does not receive.

checks.name: Training rows that duplicate another training row (from the supplied row hashes)
checks.message: 17 of 29305 training rows (0.06%) duplicate another training row. Duplicates can make a model look better on rows it has memorised and are often a data-quality problem upstream. The hashes are producer-supplied and cover the feature columns only, so rows with the same features and different labels also count as duplicates.

details.caveat: The gate does not see the training data, only its row hashes.

triggered_rules.name: Target leakage detected
triggered_rules.reason: Target leakage detected: check 'leakage.single_feature_predictiveness' is FAIL (The strongest single feature, 'prior_high_income_flag', reaches a cross-validated ROC AUC of 0.968 on its own (13 features, 9768 rows). Values near 1.0 suggest the feature leaks the label.).

decision.summary: ROLLBACK recommended: a critical rule overrides the score. MQS 85.7. Reason(s): Target leakage detected.

explanations: Decision: ROLLBACK recommended: a critical rule overrides the score. MQS 85.7. Reason(s): Target leakage detected.

Why (critical): Target leakage detected: check 'leakage.single_feature_predictiveness' is FAIL (The strongest single feature, 'prior_high_income_flag', reaches a cross-validated ROC AUC of 0.968 on its own (13 features, 9768 rows). Values near 1.0 suggest the feature leaks the label.).
Override: critical rule(s) force ROLLBACK (Target leakage detected) although the MQS of 85.7 is above the promote threshold of 75. A good score cannot outweigh a critical failure.
Weakest checks (MQS points lost): leakage.single_feature_predictiveness (-7.6), fairness.selection_rate_ratio (-5.2), behaviour.subgroup_f1_gap (-1.0), fairness.equalized_odds (-0.5).

Evidence note: these results rely on declared (unverified) producer metadata: training_validity.overfit_gap, training_validity.train_eval_overlap, training_validity.train_duplicate_rows, operational.dependency_match.
Suggested action (leakage.single_feature_predictiveness): Inspect the named feature. If it is derived from the target or only known after the outcome, remove it and retrain.
Suggested action (behaviour.subgroup_f1_gap): Examine the weakest group: check its data volume and quality, and whether features behave differently for it.

Suggested action (fairness.selection_rate_ratio): Investigate the group gap: review training-data balance and proxy features, and consider mitigation (for example reweighting or group-aware thresholds).
These suggestions are starting points, not guarantees.
